analysis.title: DeskTalk - US data back in focus as election risk clears
key_insights: ADP private payrolls rose 86k in October, comfortably above expectations, a positive sign ahead of Friday's nonfarm payrolls report where Citi economists forecast +65k, in line with consensus.
September Trade Balance narrowed to -$105.0bn, little changed from the prior month, a surprise versus expectations. Exports rose 1.9%, the strongest monthly increase in four months.
ISM Services fell to 54.5 from 54.9 in September, below expectations but still in expansion. Prices paid fell to 73.0 from 74.0, the second-highest reading since 2022.
Treasury set next week's 3y, 10y and 30y auctions at a combined $125bn, in line with expectations, at the Quarterly Refunding Announcement.
Treasury changed its coupon guidance from 'at least the next several quarters' to 'the next several quarters', which opens the door to auction size changes in 2027.
The 10y yield fell as much as ~7bps to below 4.90% after the election results, then retraced higher as event risk cleared. SPX rose ~1.8%, and the dollar is weaker but off its lows.
Citi G10 FX strategists see dips in the dollar as attractive to buy, per the note's wording. Friday's payrolls, especially average hourly earnings, feed into the December FOMC decision.
